newsitem.title: UK: Concert keen to co-operate with NTT.
newsitem.headline: Concert keen to co-operate with NTT.

text.p: Merger partners British Telecommunications Plc and MCI Communications Corp are keen to cooperate with Japanese telecom giant Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp, but don't see any talks starting soon.
Sir Peter Bonfield, BT's chief executive told the merger partners' inaugural news conference here on Sunday, "It has been no secret that at some stage I would like to deal with NTT."

But he added that the Japanese company would probably want to devote attention to the deregulation of its home market before spending energy on any overseas expansion in the fast growing Asian market.
"We have to see what comes out of that (the liberalisation of the Japanese market)," said Bonfield.
BT and NTT have already worked together for nearly 10 years in a "technology relationship".
"We work well together," said Bonfield, adding that the Concert Plc company that BT and MCI plan to create would have plenty of clout to attract Asian partnerships.
"We are a bigger player now and might look a bit more attractive to some of the Asian companies," he said.

BT in May abandoned merger talks with Cable and Wireless Plc, which would have given the former a strong foothold in Asia through its majority stake 57.5 percent stake in highly profitable Hong Kong Telecommunications.
In the end, the risks of a merger with C&W outweighed the opportunities, while the opposite was the case in a BT link-up with MCI, Bonfield said.
"This (MCI) is the first best choice," replied Bonfield to a question whether the U.S. company was second best.
